oneTimers: About $90M of non-income tax matters weighed on the quarter — Airbnb says planned investments in new growth and policy initiatives plus these tax charges are why net income fell even as revenue grew 12%.
otherDetail: Interest income of $162M, less $38M of other expense, net — a $124M net addition to profit.

segments.name: Stays & experiences
segments.note: Service fees charged to hosts and guests on every booking — Airbnb owns almost no property, so its revenue is a cut of each stay. One revenue stream.

takeaways.text: Nights and seats booked grew 10% — the strongest growth quarter of the year — and gross booking value rose 16% to $20.4B as the average daily rate climbed 6% to $168.
takeaways.title: Bookings accelerated

takeaways.text: Net income fell to $341M from $461M a year ago as planned investments in new growth and policy initiatives, plus about $90M of non-income tax matters, outweighed 12% revenue growth. Net margin fell to 12% from 19%.
takeaways.title: Profit shrank while revenue grew

takeaways.text: Airbnb's implied take rate — revenue divided by gross booking value — slipped to 13.6% from 14.1% a year ago, as it simplified fees by moving hosts to a single 15.5% service fee, alongside FX and booking-timing effects.
takeaways.title: A smaller cut of each booking

verdict: Airbnb's revenue grew 12% to $2.8B on its strongest bookings quarter of the year — 121.9 million nights and seats — but planned investments and about $90M of non-income tax charges pushed net income down to $341M, 12 cents of every revenue dollar.
